question:
An isosceles right triangle with legs of length \(8\) is partitioned into \(16\) congruent triangles as shown. The shaded area is

[Figure 1](figures/1992_AMC_8_Q10_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The 16 small triangles are congruent, so they have equal areas. The perpendicular legs of the large triangle give its base and height, making its area
\[
\frac{8\times8}{2}=32.
\]
Thus each small triangle has area \(32\div16=2\).

Count the shaded triangles in horizontal strips. From top to bottom, the strips contain \(1,2,3,4\) shaded triangles. These strips cover the figure without counting any piece twice, so there are
\[
1+2+3+4=10
\]
shaded pieces. Their total area is \(10\times2=\boxed{20}\) square units, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
